questions.question: We often refer to computer errors caused due to incorrect input data or unreliable programs as _______
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**garbage-in-garbage-out (GIGO)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **GIGO** stands for **Garbage-In-Garbage-Out**, a concept used in computing to describe how the quality of output is determined by the quality of input.
 
• If incorrect or unreliable data is entered into a system or program, the output will also be unreliable or erroneous.
 
• This concept emphasizes the importance of providing accurate and reliable data to achieve meaningful results from computer systems.
 
• The principle is a foundational idea in data processing, software development, and artificial intelligence systems.
 
• It highlights the critical role of data validation and quality control in minimizing errors in computer operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Examples of GIGO in Real Life:**

 
 
• **Spreadsheet Errors:** Entering incorrect formulas or data in a spreadsheet will lead to incorrect calculations and results.
 
• **Search Engine Results:** Poorly phrased or misspelled search queries may yield irrelevant or misleading search results.
 
• **AI Predictions:** Machine learning models trained on biased or incomplete datasets can produce inaccurate predictions or outputs.
 
 
 
• **Impact of GIGO:**
 
 
• Leads to wasted time and resources in analyzing or correcting faulty output.
 
• Can result in poor decision-making based on unreliable information.
 
• Undermines trust in automated systems and processes.
 
 
 
• **Preventing GIGO:**
 
 
• Implement robust data validation techniques to ensure input accuracy.
 
• Use automated error-checking tools to identify and correct errors in real-time.
 
• Train personnel on the importance of accurate data entry and validation.

questions.question: Which of the following is not true about the National Electronic Funds Transfer (NEFT) system?

options.text: It allows for the electronic transfer of funds between two accounts in different banks across India.
It operates on a Deferred Net Settlement (DNS) basis, where transactions are processed in batches throughout the day.
The service is only available during the traditional bank working hours, Monday to Friday.
There is no minimum or maximum limit prescribed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for the amount that can be transferred.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The service is only available during the traditional bank working hours, Monday to Friday.**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NEFT (National Electronic Funds Transfer)** is an electronic payment system that facilitates the transfer of funds between bank accounts across India on a one-to-one basis.
 
• It operates on a **Deferred Net Settlement (DNS)** basis, where transactions are processed in batches at regular intervals throughout the day.
 
• NEFT transactions can be initiated 24x7, including on weekends and bank holidays, as the system is operational round-the-clock since December 2019.
 
• There is no **minimum or maximum transaction limit** prescribed by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI), making it accessible for all types of transfers.
 
• The statement that NEFT is available only during traditional bank working hours is **incorrect**, as the service is now available 24/7 for customer convenience.

**Additional Information__**

 
• **Features of NEFT:**

 
 
• NEFT is regulated and maintained by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• Transactions are typically settled in hourly batches, ensuring timely processing of payments.
 
• It is a secure and reliable method for transferring funds within India.
 
 
 
• **Advantages of NEFT:**
 
 
• Enables individuals and businesses to make payments conveniently without physical visits to banks.
 
• Cost-effective and user-friendly, with nominal charges for transactions.
 
• Supports a wide range of transactions, including utility bill payments, loan EMIs, and more.
 
 
 
• **Key Requirements for NEFT Transactions:**
 
 
• Both the sender and recipient must have a bank account.
 
• The sender must provide details such as the recipient's name, account number, bank branch, and IFSC code.
 
• NEFT is only applicable for Indian Rupee transactions within India.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• NEFT is different from RTGS (Real-Time Gross Settlement), which processes transactions in real-time but requires a minimum transfer amount.
 
• NEFT is ideal for small to medium-value transactions, while RTGS is preferred for high-value transfers.
 
• Transactions initiated outside banking hours are processed in the next available batch.

questions.question: Which of the following keyboard shortcuts on a Windows 10 home screen opens the item's properties?
questions.solution:
__**Explanation:**__

**Alt + Enter**

The **Alt + Enter** keyboard shortcut in Windows 10 is used to open the properties of a selected item, such as a file, folder, or shortcut, on the home screen or in File Explorer. This shortcut provides a quick way to access detailed information about the selected item, including its size, location, security settings, and other attributes. Here’s how it works:

__
 
• Select the desired item (file, folder, or shortcut) on the Windows 10 home screen or in File Explorer.
 
• Press the **Alt** key and the **Enter** key simultaneously.
 
• The item's Properties window will appear, displaying all relevant details.

This functionality is particularly useful when you want to quickly check or modify the attributes or permissions of a file or folder without navigating through multiple menus. The **Alt + Enter** shortcut is a standard feature in Windows operating systems and enhances user productivity by streamlining access to important information.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

To further understand the analysis, let’s evaluate the other options:

**Option 1: Insert + Alt**

This combination is not a recognized shortcut for accessing item properties in Windows 10. It does not perform any specific action related to file or folder properties and is, therefore, incorrect for this context.

**Option 2: F2 + Alt**

The **F2** key is generally used for renaming a selected item in Windows. However, combining it with **Alt** does not trigger any specific functionality related to opening properties. This option is invalid.

**Option 3: Tab + Del**

The **Tab** key is primarily used for navigating between elements or fields in a user interface, while the **Del** key is used for deleting items. Combining these keys does not result in opening the properties of an item, making this option incorrect.

questions.question:
Which of the given statements is true?

i) SRAM is slower than DRAM.

ii) DRAM uses capacitors and a few transistors.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **SRAM (Static Random Access Memory) is faster than DRAM (Dynamic Random Access Memory).**
 
• SRAM is primarily used in applications requiring high-speed memory, such as CPU caches, whereas DRAM is used for main memory due to its higher density and lower cost.
 
• **DRAM uses capacitors to store data in the form of electrical charges and requires periodic refreshing to retain the data.**
 
• In contrast, SRAM uses flip-flops made of multiple transistors to store data and does not require refreshing, leading to faster access times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Statement (i):** "SRAM is slower than DRAM" is incorrect because SRAM is faster than DRAM.
 
• **Statement (ii):** "DRAM uses capacitors and a few transistors" is correct. DRAM stores data using capacitors and requires refreshing to maintain the data.
 
• **Conclusion:** Since only statement (ii) is correct, the correct answer is Option 4__.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT an operating system for mobile phones?

The correct answer is __**Unix.**__

• **iOS:** iOS is Apple's mobile operating system used for devices such as iPhones and iPads. It is known for its smooth user interface and security features.
 
• **webOS:** webOS is an operating system initially developed by Palm Inc. for smartphones. It is now used in LG smart TVs but is categorized as a mobile operating system.
 
• **Unix:** Unix is a multi-user, multitasking operating system primarily used for servers and workstations. It is not specifically designed for mobile phones, which makes it the correct answer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following refers to a huge database of internet resources such as webpages, newsgroups, programs, images etc., and helps to locate information on the World Wide Web?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Search engine**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **search engine** is an online tool designed to help users locate information available on the **World Wide Web (WWW)**.
 
• It works by indexing vast amounts of data, including **webpages, images, videos, news articles, and other internet resources**, and retrieving relevant results based on a user’s query.
 
• Popular examples of search engines include **Google, Bing, Yahoo!, DuckDuckGo, and Baidu**.
 
• Search engines utilize algorithms to determine the most relevant results for a user’s query by analyzing factors like keywords, backlinks, user behavior, and content quality.
 
• They are essential tools for navigating the internet, making it easier to access information quickly and efficiently.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Web Browser:**

 
 
• A web browser is a software application used to access and display webpages and other content on the internet.
 
• Examples include **Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Safari, and Microsoft Edge**.
 
• Unlike search engines, browsers do not index or retrieve data but instead render content from specific URLs entered by the user.
 
 
 
• **Website:**
 
 
• A website is a collection of related content, such as text, images, and other multimedia, hosted on a web server and accessible via a unique URL.
 
• Examples of websites include **Amazon, Wikipedia, and Netflix**.
 
• Websites are the resources that search engines index and display as search results.
 
 
 
• **Web Server:**
 
 
• A web server is a computer system that stores, processes, and delivers webpages to users over the internet.
 
• It works by responding to HTTP or HTTPS requests from web browsers or search engines.
 
• Popular web server software includes **Apache, Nginx, and Microsoft IIS**.
 
 
 
• **Working of Search Engines:**
 
 
• **Crawling:** Search engines use bots or spiders to traverse the internet and discover content on various websites.
 
• **Indexing:** The discovered content is analyzed and stored in a database to make it searchable.
 
• **Ranking:** Search engines use algorithms to rank results based on relevance, keyword usage, and quality of content.

questions.question: Which of the following applications can help you NOT to create a file?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Windows Explorer**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Windows Explorer** is a file management system used in Microsoft Windows operating systems to browse and manage files and folders.
 
• It allows users to view, copy, move, rename, and delete files or folders but does not provide tools for creating new files directly within the interface.
 
• Unlike other applications such as MS-Word or Notepad, Windows Explorer is not designed to generate or edit content within files.
 
• Its primary function is to serve as a user-friendly interface for organizing and accessing files stored on a computer or connected storage devices.
 
• Windows Explorer is now known as **File Explorer** in modern versions of Windows, starting from Windows 8.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Paint:**

 
 
• Paint is a basic graphics editing application included in Microsoft Windows operating systems.
 
• It enables users to create and edit images, including the ability to save them as files in different formats such as BMP, JPEG, PNG, and GIF.
 
• Users can draw, color, and manipulate pictures with tools such as brushes, shapes, and text.
 
 
 
• **Notepad:**
 
 
• Notepad is a simple text editor available in Windows operating systems.
 
• It allows users to create, edit, and save plain text files with the extension ".txt".
 
• Notepad is often used for creating or editing lightweight text documents, scripts, or code snippets.
 
 
 
• **MS-Word:**
 
 
• MS-Word, or Microsoft Word, is a word processing software developed by Microsoft.
 
• It allows users to create, edit, and format text-based documents such as letters, resumes, and reports.
 
• Documents can be saved in various formats, including DOCX and PDF, and include advanced tools for styling, layout, and collaboration.

questions.question: Which of the following is used to access programs, files and settings in Windows 7?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Start Button**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Start Button in Windows 7 is the primary way to access programs, files, and settings on the computer.
 
• It is located on the lower-left corner of the screen within the taskbar, making it easily accessible for users.
 
• By clicking the Start Button, users can open the Start Menu, which provides access to frequently used applications, a search bar for quick navigation, and links to system settings and files.
 
• The Start Menu is divided into two main panels: the left panel shows pinned and recently used applications, while the right panel provides access to libraries, control panel, devices, and network connections.
 
• The Start Button also allows users to log off, shut down, restart, or put the computer to sleep.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taskbar:**

 
 
• The taskbar is a horizontal bar at the bottom of the Windows desktop that allows users to switch between open applications and access pinned programs quickly.
 
• It contains the Start Button, system tray, notification area, and shortcuts to frequently used programs.
 
• Although the taskbar provides access to applications, it does not offer features like searching for files or system settings directly.
 
 
 
• **Control Panel:**
 
 
• The Control Panel is a component of Microsoft Windows that provides centralized access to configure system settings and manage hardware or software.
 
• It includes options for managing user accounts, adjusting display settings, installing/uninstalling programs, and configuring network settings.
 
• While it is a powerful tool for system management, it is not used for accessing general applications or files.
 
 
 
• **Notification Area:**
 
 
• The notification area, also known as the system tray, is located on the right side of the taskbar in Windows.
 
• It displays system notifications, clock, and status icons for certain applications like antivirus software, volume control, and network connectivity.
 
• The notification area is not designed for accessing files, programs, or system settings directly.

questions.question: To adjust the screen resolution or change the desktop background in Windows, which of the following would a user typically access?

__
 
• To adjust the screen resolution or change the desktop background in Windows, users typically need to access the **Settings** menu.
 
• The **Settings** menu is a centralized location in Windows where users can customize various system preferences, including display settings, sound, network, and personalization options.
 
• To access the Settings menu, users can click on the Start button and select the **"Settings"** gear icon or press the **Windows + I** shortcut keys.
 
• Within the Settings menu, the **"System" section** includes options for adjusting display resolution, scaling, and layout.
 
• The **"Personalization" section** within Settings allows users to change desktop backgrounds, themes, colors, and lock screen preferences.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **This PC**

 
 
• The **"This PC"** option (formerly known as "My Computer") provides access to the file explorer where users can view and manage drives, folders, and files on their computer.
 
 
 
• **Documents**
 
 
• The **"Documents"** folder is a default directory in Windows for saving and organizing personal and work-related files.
 
 
 
• **Run**
 
 
• The **"Run"** dialog box is used to execute commands, open applications, and access specific system utilities by entering command-line instructions.

questions.question: When a plain text email is sent, which Content-Type value is typically specified in the message header, according to MIME standards?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**text/plain; charset=UTF-8**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **text/plain** is the default MIME Content-Type for plain text email messages.
 
• The **charset=UTF-8** specification ensures support for a wide range of characters, including international ones.
 
• MIME (Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions) standards define how email content is formatted and transmitted.
 
• Plain text emails are simple and do not contain formatting, such as bold or italic text, images, or hyperlinks.
 
• Plain text is widely used for compatibility across email clients and platforms, ensuring readability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **MIME Content-Type Terminology:**

 
 
• **text/plain**: Specifies unformatted text content.
 
• **text/html**: Indicates HTML-formatted text, allowing rich formatting and multimedia elements.
 
• **multipart/mixed**: Used for emails containing multiple parts, such as text and attachments.
 
• **application/octet-stream**: Represents binary data, typically used for file attachments.
 
 
 
• **Charset:**
 
 
• Defines the character encoding used in the email.
 
• **UTF-8** is the most widely used encoding, supporting virtually all characters across languages.
 
 
 
• **Plain Text vs HTML Emails:**
 
 
• Plain text emails are lightweight and universally compatible.
 
• HTML emails allow for visually appealing designs but may not render correctly in all email clients.
 
 
 
• **Email Header:**
 
 
• Contains metadata about the email, such as sender, recipient, and Content-Type.
 
• The Content-Type header specifies the format of the message body.
